name: Mazindol
summary: Mazindol, sold under the brand names Mazanor and Sanorex, is an appetite suppressant which is used in the short-term treatment of obesity. It is also used off-label in the treatment of narcolepsy and cataplexy. The drug is taken orally.

pharmacology.text: Mazindol is a sympathomimetic amine, which is similar to amphetamine. It stimulates the central nervous system, which increases heart rate and blood pressure, and decreases appetite. Sympathomimetic anoretics (appetite suppressants) are used in the short-term treatment of obesity. Their appetite-reducing effect tends to decrease after a few weeks of treatment.
pharmacology.kind: Serotonin–norepinephrine–dopamine reuptake inhibitor (SNDRI); Anorectic; Wakefulness-promoting agent; Stimulant

uses.text: Mazindol is used in short-term (i.e., a few weeks) treatment of obesity, in combination with a regimen of weight reduction based on caloric restriction, exercise, and behavior modification in people with a body mass index greater than 30, or in those with a body mass index greater than 27 in the presence of risk factors such as hypertension, diabetes, or hyperlipidemia.
